title: Extension by zero preserves the finite-Tor constructible category
statement:
Use the standing finite-field, coefficient and finite-type scheme conventions of [sk-def-sf-operations]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes admitting a compactification, and let $a\le b$ be integers. Use the small pro-étale coefficient categories: finite coefficients, derived-complete integral coefficients, raw rationalization, and the common finite-stage category, as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, let $K\in\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ have cohomology concentrated in $[a,b]$ and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. At $\mathcal O_E$ the latter means that every derived finite reduction has Tor amplitude in this same interval, independently of the reduction exponent. Then $Rj_!K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ has cohomology concentrated in $[a,b]$ and the same Tor interval.

At $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $\Dctf=\Dbc$ by definition, $Rj_!$ preserves $\Dbc$ and every cohomological interval $[a,b]$, with the interval interpreted by the standard pairs of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. No additional numerical Tor-interval condition is defined at these two stages by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Thus extension by zero carries $\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ at every coefficient stage, without changing any interval asserted above.

proof.text: Keep the scheme and coefficient conventions of [sk-def-sf-operations]; in particular no separatedness of $U$ or $Y$ is added. The finite-type schemes are Noetherian: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (its ring has just the ideals $0,k$), so apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [def-weil-constructible-subset] every subset of their underlying Noetherian spaces is retrocompact. Hence for each affine open $V\subset Y$, $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact, so $j$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $J$ for termwise extension by zero, initially over either the constant finite ring sheaf or the completed integral ring sheaf $B_Y$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] the open site is the localized site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$; at integral coefficients [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] defines $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_T$. Limits of module sheaves are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], and their ring operations are componentwise. Thus on each $V\to U$ both $B_Y|_U$ and $B_U$ are the same compatible families of finite-coefficient sections, by the constant-coefficient identification in the localization lemma. This identifies $B_Y|_U=B_U$ and every finite projection, so the coefficient rings agree, not just their scalar rings of global sections. The ringed-site lemma [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives exactness of $J$ and restriction, and their adjunction. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $J$ acts termwise on derived categories. For every complex $C$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^r(JC)\cong JH^r(C)$. In particular $J$ preserves every cohomological vanishing interval, since an additive functor sends zero to zero.

proof.text:
First prove finite-stage bounded constructibility without any finite-Tor assumption, since integral representatives used later need this stronger formulation. For a constructible $A_{E,n}$-module sheaf $F$ on $U$, choose its finite locally closed constructible partition $U=\coprod_
u S_
u$ from [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Each $S_
u$ remains locally closed in $Y$: write $S_
u=O\cap C$ with $O$ open in $U$ and $C$ closed in $U$ by [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]; then $O$ is open in $Y$, $C=U\cap C'$ for $C'$ closed in $Y$, and $S_
u=O\cap C'$. With its given locally closed subscheme structure this is the same stratum. Add the reduced closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ constructed by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](2). Step 1 and [def-weil-constructible-subset] make all these strata constructible in $Y$. The arbitrary-ringed pro-étale identities [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], with the quasi-compact $j$ of step 1, give $j^*JF\cong F$ and $i^*JF=0$ as module sheaves. If $s:S_
u	o U$ is a stratum, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the exact finite-coefficient pullback in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] identify $(j\circ s)^*JF$ with $s^*F$. The coefficient identifications satisfy the required composition hypothesis: both identifications send a local constant scalar $a\in A_{E,n}$ to that same scalar, and constant sections generate the constant sheaf locally. Thus on $S_
u$ the restriction is the original finite locally constant sheaf and on $Z$ it is the zero sheaf, constant with finite zero module. This partition witnesses constructibility of $JF$. Apply this separately to every nonzero $H^r(C)$ of an arbitrary bounded constructible finite-stage complex $C$. The exact cohomology formula of step 1 proves bounded constructibility of $JC$ with every original cohomological interval. No common-refinement assertion or geometric-stalk conservativity is needed. For a finite-Tor $C$, the existing same-unit theorem [lem-trf-open-ctf] additionally gives preservation of each chosen Tor interval. In particular it applies to $K$ in the statement and, below, to each finite reduction of an integral finite-Tor $K$; its cohomological and Tor intervals need not coincide.

proof.text:
We need a ringed calculation to pass to integral coefficients. For a sheaf of commutative rings $B$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives $JP\otimes_B M\cong J(P\otimes_{B|_U}M|_U)$ for module sheaves. Apply this in each bidegree of the tensor complexes of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The adjunction of step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] imply that $J$ preserves the small direct sums in each total degree. Thus the same identity holds on total tensor complexes, with the same differentials and signs. Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to C$ over $B|_U$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For any acyclic $B$-complex $Q$, restriction $Q|_U$ is acyclic by step 1, $P\otimes Q|_U$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], and its exact extension by zero is acyclic by step 1. The tensor identity therefore proves that $JP$ is K-flat, directly from that definition. For a ring-sheaf map $B\to B'$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] now computes both scalar extensions on these K-flat representatives and gives
$$(JC)\otimes_B^LB'\cong J_{B'}(C\otimes_{B|_U}^LB'|_U).$$
This is an isomorphism of $B'$-complexes: on the sheaf tensor identity the $B'$-action on each side is multiplication on the $B'$ factor. It is natural in $C$ and in $B'$, since the underived tensor identity is natural and the representative maps are $1\otimes\rho$ for $\rho:B'\to B''$. In particular, with $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $B'=(A_{E,n})_Y$, [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] gives $(JC)_n\cong J_n(C_n)$, compatibly with the transition maps induced by $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$. Restriction of scalars commutes with $J$ here because [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] uses the same summands and maps, and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] sheafifies the underlying abelian presheaf and extends its module action uniquely.

proof.text: Let $K\in\Dctf(U,\mathcal O_E)$. Its integral constructibility means derived completeness and finite constructibility of all $K_n$, with one cohomological interval $[c,d]$ independent of $n$, by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Its Tor hypothesis means one interval $[a,b]$ for every $K_n$, by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The completeness assertion of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] uses Koszul completeness [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], whereas the integral category uses quotient-tower completeness [def-weil-derived-complete]. The final paragraph of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], applied on the small pro-étale site with the completed coefficient sheaf, identifies the two completion functors and their units. To justify this even for the object-only Roos formulation, [def-weil-derived-complete] first gives an isomorphism of $K$ with its quotient-tower limit. The comparison identifies this limit with the Koszul completion, whose output satisfies the local completeness condition by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]. That condition is invariant under isomorphism, so $K$ satisfies it. The reflector theorem now makes the natural Koszul unit of $K$ invertible, exactly the completeness hypothesis of the extension theorem. This does not assume uniqueness of a lift to an arbitrary Roos triangle. Apply that theorem to the identity cartesian open square, then use the same comparison on $Y$ to conclude that $JK$ is complete in the quotient-tower sense required here. Both theorems are applied to the actual completed coefficient sheaf: since every $A_{E,n}$ is finite, the final sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] identifies the sheafified constant ring sheaf $(A_{E,n})_T$ with the coefficient sheaf $(P_n)_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], compatibly with the quotient maps, hence $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=A_T$ for $T=U,Y$ and the module categories coincide. Its coefficient hypotheses [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] hold for $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi_E))$: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives a Noetherian domain and a finite residue field; [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] gives all finite quotients. Each quotient has the two-term finite free resolution $\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}\mathcal O_E$, injective because $\varpi_E\ne0$ in a domain, so it is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; its additive group is finite and hence torsion. The geometric hypothesis is the quasi-compactness of $j$ verified in step 1. By step 3 the reductions of $JK$ are $J_nK_n$. Step 2 makes these constructible, keeps their uniform cohomological interval $[c,d]$, and keeps their Tor interval $[a,b]$. These are exactly the conditions in the two definitions cited above, so $JK\in\Dctf(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Independently of $[c,d]$, the actual cohomological interval $[a,b]$ of the integral $K$ is retained by the exact cohomology calculation in step 1. The same argument also proves the integral bounded-constructible preservation needed below without a finite-Tor hypothesis: start with any $K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$, retain its derived completeness and uniformly bounded constructible reductions, omit only the Tor-interval sentences, and conclude $JK\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. This version still preserves every actual integral upper or lower cohomological bound by step 1.

proof.text: Identify these functors with the $Rj_!$ of the statement. At finite coefficients choose the compactification $U\xrightarrow{j}Y\xrightarrow{1_Y}Y$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Its compact-support candidate is $R(1_Y)_*J=J$: the identity sheaf functor is exact, and applying it to a K-injective resolution computes the identity derived functor. Bounded constructibility supplies a bounded-below étale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Thus [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] identifies this candidate with the one for any chosen compactification on precisely the required domain. At the integral stage [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] defines $Rj_!K$ as the derived limit of the restricted-scalar finite images $J_nK_n$, with the reduction transitions. Step 3 identifies this tower, including its maps, with the reduction tower of $JK$. Completeness in step 4, interpreted by [def-weil-derived-complete], identifies $JK$ with a derived limit of this tower, so the two objects are isomorphic. For later rationalization the identification must also be natural, rather than an unrelated choice of a Roos triangle for every object. Use the functorial completion and unit in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]: its final paragraph identifies the quotient-tower limit with the Koszul completion, respecting the units. The unit $JK\to (JK)^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ is a natural isomorphism on these complete objects; composing it with that comparison and the natural strict-tower identification of step 3 gives a natural isomorphism $J\cong Rj_!$ on the integral constructible category. All maps are module-linear, as is the tower comparison, so this isomorphism is $\mathcal O_E$-linear as well. Consequently all membership and vanishing assertions proved for $J$ are assertions for $Rj_!$; no independence on arbitrary nonconstructible pro-étale complexes has been used.

source.place: Rj_! interpreted through the trivial compactification and the existing finite/integral definitions; finite independence on bounded-below étale-origin objects only

proof.text: At $E$ coefficients use the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Extension by zero is $\mathcal O_E$-linear: on the presheaf each nonzero value has the given scalar action and zero has its zero action, and sheafification preserves these module maps. Hence its rational functor sends $f\otimes e$ to $J(f)\otimes e$; balancing, identities and composition follow from this linearity. The natural $\mathcal O_E$-linear identification of step 5 rationalizes on Hom tensors, so by [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] this is naturally isomorphic to the prescribed rational compact-support operation. The bounded-constructible preservation in the final sentence of step 4 ensures its object lies in $\Dbc(Y,E)$. To check an upper bound $b$, [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] supplies an integral object $L$ with no cohomology above $b$ and an isomorphism $K_E\cong QL$ in the rational category. This upper-bound witness is not required to have the lower bound or the original integral representative. Exactness from step 1 gives the same upper bound for $JL$; its constructibility follows by the integral argument in step 4 without its Tor-bound clause (all reductions remain bounded constructible uniformly). Applying the rational functor to the witnessing isomorphism gives $Rj_!K_E\cong QJL$. For the lower bound, choose separately an integral $L_-$ with no cohomology below $a$ and an isomorphism $K_E\cong QL_-$. Step 1 gives $H^r(JL_-)=0$ for $r<a$, steps 2–4 without the Tor clause give its integral constructibility, and applying the rational functor gives $Rj_!K_E\cong QJL_-$. The use of bounds $a,b$ through shifts is legitimate: the termwise functor commutes with shifts by the shift clause of the exact-derived-functor theorem in step 1, and this compatibility rationalizes. The standard pair therefore puts $Rj_!K_E$ in the same interval $[a,b]$. At this stage $\Dctf=\Dbc$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; there is no inference that every arbitrary pro-étale module over a topological coefficient field is flat.

source.place: Coefficient-stage interpretation via the rationalization and standard-pair definitions; upper and lower bounds use separate integral witnesses

proof.text: Finally [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents each common-stage object by a pair $(E,K_E)$, and [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] sends it to $(E,Rj_!K_E)$. The coefficient compatibilities of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] ensure that this is the prescribed operation when one changes the finite field of definition. Its constructibility follows at that finite stage from step 6. For either cohomological bound, [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] gives an isomorphism to a pair at a finite stage possessing that bound; apply the functor to the isomorphism and use step 6 at that stage. Explicitly, for an upper-bound witness $K\cong (L,M_+)$ with $M_+\in D_c^{\le b}(U,L)$, its image is isomorphic to $(L,Rj_!M_+)$, whose upper bound is step 6. For a separate lower-bound witness $K\cong (L',M_-)$ with $M_-\in D_c^{\ge a}(U,L')$, the image is isomorphic to $(L',Rj_!M_-)$ and has the lower bound by step 6. The common-stage shift is represented by the finite-stage shift, so these are precisely the two inequalities of the standard pair. Since [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] defines $\Dctf=\Dbc$ at common-stage coefficients, this completes the preservation assertion at all stages. The zero complex and empty open require no special argument: exact extension by zero sends them to zero, and all the intervals remain valid.
